question: A complex SQL query is taking 30 seconds to execute on a table with 10 million rows. Walk through your optimization process and techniques.

keyPoints: Use EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE to understand query execution plan
Add appropriate indexes on WHERE, JOIN, ORDER BY columns - consider composite indexes
Check for full table scans, inefficient joins, missing statistics
Optimize query structure: avoid SELECT *, eliminate subqueries, use joins instead of IN
Consider partitioning large tables, materialized views for complex aggregations
Analyze index selectivity and cardinality to ensure indexes are effective
expectedAnswer.explanation: Optimization process: (1) Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE to see actual execution plan and identify bottlenecks (Seq Scan, nested loops on large tables). (2) Add covering indexes for WHERE/JOIN predicates - composite index (customer_id, order_date) better than separate indexes. (3) Rewrite query: replace IN subquery with JOIN (better optimizer opportunities), specify needed columns only (reduces data transfer), add LIMIT if appropriate. (4) Update table statistics (ANALYZE) so optimizer makes better decisions. (5) For very large tables, consider partitioning by date range. (6) Use materialized views for expensive aggregations run repeatedly. Monitor query performance continuously and adjust as data grows.

followUps: When might adding an index actually hurt performance?
Explain the difference between covering index and composite index.
